title: Hardware matrix: end-to-end latency & cost-per-token synthesis with p95/regression hooks
creator: Maya Patel
description: Synthesize a repeatable hardware matrix benchmark that measures end-to-end latency (including network and pre/post-processing), tokens/sec, and cost-per-token across A10, L4, A100, and H100 instances. The goal is to produce an automated report and CI gate that detects p95 regressions and triggers triage runbooks. Unlike previous throughput-only sweeps, this ticket targets tail behavior, variance under realistic burst patterns, and cost-normalized comparisons for multiple model sizes and quantization profiles.
approach: Define representative workloads: interactive short prompts, long-context generation, batched inference, and embedding micro-bursts
Standardize measurement harness to capture full request lifecycle: client -> network -> runtime -> postproc; include synthetic and replayed production traces
Run across hardware matrix (A10/L4/A100/H100) for each model variant (fp16, int8, q4_0 where supported) and for batching configs {none, 8, 32, dynamic}
Measure latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, GPU occupancy, and compute a cost-per-token using region-specific pricing and reserved vs burst pricing assumptions
Integrate regression detection: baseline rollups, rolling p95 thresholds, bootstrap confidence intervals, and automated alerting to the performance channel when regressions exceed thresholds
Publish synthesized report, CSVs, dashboards, and a CI job that runs a lighter sweep on PRs that touch the runtime/kernel selection layer
workloads: long-context-32k: evaluate memory and kv-cache effects (where supported)
burst-replay: 90/10 burst pattern replayed from production traces
hardware_matrix: NVIDIA A10 (24GB) - tuned for cost-sensitive inference
NVIDIA H100 (80GB/94GB) - peak throughput and long-context profiles
automation: Benchmark harness implemented as a parametrized runner in infra/bench; outputs parquet/CSV and uploads to S3. CI-lite job triggers on runtime PRs; full sweep scheduled nightly. Regression detector computes bootstrapped p95 confidence intervals and posts alerts to #perf-alerts with a link to an automated bisect workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Automated harness can run the defined workloads across all four hardware types and produce consistent CSV outputs
Dashboards (Grafana) show p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-token for each model/hardware/batch configuration
Regression detector runs on nightly sweep and on PRs, with reproducible alert links to the failed run and suggested owner
A one-page synthesized cost-vs-latency recommendation exists for customers: recommended hardware by workload and quantization profile
Docs/confluence page with run instructions, interpretation guide, and known limitations published
notes: Trade-offs: including network adds realism but increases run-to-run variance; we mitigate with 30-run sampling and bootstrapping
Known limitation: L4 driver for long-context >16k is flaky in current infra image; will use kernel fallback and mark results accordingly
Follow-ups: add region price curves (reserved vs spot) and slot-level amortized infra cost
Security review: no customer data in this sweep; replay traces sanitized. Security review planned if using production traces unsanitized
